limitations_and_boundaries: The proposed methods are nonparametric, with no hard restrictions on data distributions and causal mechanisms, and do not rely on window segmentation.
CD-NOD can find causal direction between even two variables, thanks to the surrogate variable C or the independent change property.
Bayesian change point detection can only be applied to detect changes in marginal or joint distributions, whereas causal mechanisms are represented by conditional distributions.
The linear time-dependent GP requires the assumption of linearity and fails to handle changes in noise distributions.
CD-NOD may not identify some causal directions if identifiability conditions are not satisfied (Theorem 2).
The method is extended to allow both time-varying lagged and instantaneous causal relationships.
Distribution shifts also help for causal discovery when there exist stationary confounders.
Heterogeneity/nonstationarity and soft intervention are related in causal discovery.
